key_insight: PDE foundation models pretrained on fluid-centric data struggle to generalize to extreme-loading material dynamics dominated by shocks, evolving interfaces, and fracture; benchmarking on two discontinuity-heavy regimes quantifies this out-of-distribution transfer gap.
problem_solved: Clarifies how well (or poorly) fluid-trained PDE foundation models transfer to material-dynamics tasks with strong discontinuities and failure mechanisms—an important unknown for designers who might reuse such models outside their training domain.
method: Define two challenging downstream regimes that produce highly non-smooth fields: shock-driven perturbed layered interface (PLI) and dynamic fracture/failure evolution (FRAC).

Benchmark out-of-distribution transfer by evaluating PDE foundation models pretrained on fluid-centric datasets on these regimes, formulating the downstream task as terminal-state (final-snapshot) prediction.
Compare performance (errors, qualitative field reconstructions) to appropriate baselines and assess where pretrained models fail or require adaptation.
impact: Provides practical, quantitative guidance on the limits of reusing fluid-pretrained PDE models for extreme material dynamics, informing whether to fine-tune, collect specialized data, or develop new architectures for discontinuity-rich domains.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram contrasting the two test regimes: PLI (layered materials + shock) vs FRAC (crack initiation and propagation).
Side-by-side field visualizations (ground truth vs model prediction) highlighting failure modes and error hotspots near shocks/interfaces/fractures.
Bar/line chart showing performance drop (error or accuracy) of fluid-pretrained models on in-distribution vs out-of-distribution tasks.
Heatmap or scatter plot mapping error as a function of discontinuity strength (e.g., shock Mach number or fracture energy) to illustrate where transfer breaks down.
paper_title: Out-of-distribution transfer of PDE foundation models to material dynamics under extreme loading
paper_authors: Mahindra Rautela, Alexander Most, Siddharth Mansingh, Aleksandra Pachalieva, Bradley Love
